subject: Food Science
title: Scurvy and Vitamin C
description: A fast breakdown of Scurvy and Vitamin C for builders.

hook.text: Between 1500 and 1800, scurvy killed more sailors than all wars, storms, and other diseases combined.

buildup.text: Scurvy collapses collagen production: gums bleed, teeth fall out, wounds reopen, and bones weaken.

discovery.text: In 1747, James Lind conducted history's first clinical trial—giving 12 sailors 6 different treatments.

twist.text: Despite Lind's proof, the British Navy waited 42 years before mandating lime juice in 1795.

climax.text: Vitamin C wasn't isolated until 1932 by Albert Szent-Györgyi—185 years after Lind's experiment.

punchline.text: The cure was lemons. The proof took one trial. The navy took 42 years.

quiz.question: How long after Lind proved citrus cured scurvy did the navy mandate it?
options: 42 years—thousands more sailors died after the cure was already known
